pipeline.data_validation: Load image identifiers and binary labels from metadata, verify that labeled images can be decoded as RGB, and inspect the class distribution before constructing the stratified split; the evidenced data had roughly 75% positive examples.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No model ensemble or probability calibration is evidenced. Use sigmoid probabilities from the validation-selected checkpoint.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not apply stochastic training augmentation to validation or test data. Near-perfect holdout AUC can conceal shortcut learning or overconfidence, so inspect class-conditional prediction distributions and do not infer robustness from training loss alone.
pipeline.feature_representation: Resize images to 256x256, normalize with ImageNet statistics, and apply random horizontal flips, rotations, and color jitter during training; use deterministic resize and normalization for validation and test images.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: An all-data refit is not evidenced. Reload the checkpoint with the best validation AUC and run deterministic preprocessing and batched sigmoid inference on every test image.
pipeline.model_stack: Fine-tune an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 end to end with adaptive pooling, dropout, and a single-logit binary classification head.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single holdout. Retain probabilities from the fixed 15% validation partition for model selection and diagnostic AUC only.
pipeline.split_validation: Create one stratified 85/15 train-validation split. Apply stochastic augmentation only to the training partition and evaluate untouched validation images with ROC-AUC.
pipeline.training_protocol: Optimize focal loss with gamma 2.0 and alpha 0.75 using AdamW, cosine annealing, automatic mixed precision, and early stopping with patience 5 based on validation ROC-AUC.

nodes.title: End-to-End EfficientNet-B0 with Focal Loss and Strong Augmentation
nodes.when_to_use: Use as a strong, compute-efficient pretrained baseline when the training set is moderately imbalanced and one GPU can support 256x256 end-to-end fine-tuning.

pipeline.data_validation: Load identifiers and binary targets from the labeled metadata, verify image decoding, and check positive and negative counts before splitting so stratification preserves the observed imbalance.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No cross-model ensemble or explicit calibration is evidenced. CutMix is a training regularizer, not an inference ensemble.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Mixed CutMix targets are valid for loss computation but must not replace binary labels in ROC-AUC evaluation. If holdout AUC reaches 1.0 within a few epochs or prediction probabilities collapse toward one class, treat this as a shortcut-learning warning rather than evidence for longer training.
pipeline.feature_representation: Resize to 256x256 and normalize with ImageNet statistics. For training, apply random flips, rotations or affine transforms, color jitter, random erasing, and batch-level CutMix.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: An all-data refit is not evidenced. Restore the best holdout checkpoint and infer once per deterministically transformed test image, converting logits to probabilities with sigmoid.
pipeline.model_stack: Fine-tune all layers of an ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B2. Feed its 1408-dimensional representation to a 256-unit nonlinear head with dropout and one output logit.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single holdout. Compute ROC-AUC only from unmixed binary validation labels and their predicted probabilities.
pipeline.split_validation: Use one stratified 80/20 train-validation split. Keep validation preprocessing deterministic and select the checkpoint by validation ROC-AUC with patience-5 early stopping.
pipeline.training_protocol: Use AdamW with differential learning rates of 5e-5 for the backbone and 1e-3 for the head, label-smoothed BCE, mixed precision, gradient clipping, linear warmup followed by cosine annealing, and at most 30 epochs.

nodes.title: EfficientNet-B2 Fine-Tuning with Differential Learning Rates and CutMix
nodes.when_to_use: Use when EfficientNet-B0 has saturated and additional capacity is affordable, while strong regularization is needed to control rapid overfitting on the small, easy image task.

pipeline.data_validation: Read image identifiers and binary labels, verify that both classes are represented and images decode correctly, then preserve class proportions in the validation partition.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: At inference, average probabilities from the original image, horizontal flip, vertical flip, and combined horizontal-vertical flip. No explicit probability calibration or multi-model ensemble is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: The higher-capacity backbone can memorize this near-separable task despite augmentation. Stop on AUC rather than training loss, and ensure geometric TTA is applied consistently before averaging probabilities.
pipeline.feature_representation: Resize images to 256x256 and normalize with ImageNet statistics. Apply random 90-degree rotation, horizontal and vertical flips, and color jitter to training images; additionally apply batch-level CutMix.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: An all-data refit is not evidenced. Reload the validation-selected checkpoint, generate the four deterministic TTA views for each test image, apply sigmoid, and average the four probabilities.
pipeline.model_stack: Fine-tune an ImageNet-pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny with a classifier composed of LayerNorm, a 768-to-256 linear projection, GELU, dropout, and a final single-logit layer.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single holdout. Use the fixed validation partition for ROC-AUC checkpoint selection; no full out-of-fold prediction set is supported.
pipeline.split_validation: Use a stratified 85/15 train-validation split. Monitor validation ROC-AUC, retain the best checkpoint, and stop after 10 epochs without improvement.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train with label-smoothed BCE, AdamW, a 5% linear learning-rate warmup followed by cosine annealing, mixed precision, and gradient accumulation when needed to reach an effective batch size of 128.

nodes.title: ConvNeXt-Tiny with CutMix, Warmup-Cosine Training, and Four-View TTA
nodes.when_to_use: Use when more model capacity than EfficientNet-B0 is desired and memory permits 256x256 ConvNeXt training, especially when regularization and inference-time flip invariance are important.

pipeline.data_validation: Load labeled image identifiers, verify binary targets and decodable RGB images, and inspect class counts before creating a stratified partition.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Average probabilities from the original and horizontally flipped image at validation or test inference. No multi-seed ensemble or explicit calibration is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: The 64x64 representation may discard fine spatial detail, so this design should not be assumed equivalent to higher-resolution backbones. Keep mixed targets confined to training loss and use original binary labels for validation AUC.
pipeline.feature_representation: Resize to 64x64, normalize using ImageNet statistics, and augment training images with horizontal flips, rotation, affine transformations, color jitter, and MixUp.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: An all-data refit is not evidenced. Restore the best validation checkpoint, predict the original and horizontal-flip test views, apply sigmoid, and average the two probabilities.
pipeline.model_stack: Replace the classifier of an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 with a single-logit binary head and fine-tune the pretrained representation in two stages.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single holdout. Select the model from one stratified validation partition; do not describe its validation predictions as full OOF predictions.
pipeline.split_validation: Create one stratified train-validation split. Evaluate deterministic validation images with ROC-AUC and use patience-5 early stopping to select the best checkpoint.
pipeline.training_protocol: Freeze the backbone for the first five epochs, then unfreeze it at a reduced learning rate. Use label-smoothed BCE with smoothing 0.05, AdamW, cosine annealing, mixed precision, MixUp, and early stopping.

nodes.title: Staged ResNet-18 Fine-Tuning with MixUp and Flip TTA
nodes.when_to_use: Use as a smaller pretrained alternative when compute is constrained, 64x64 inputs are acceptable, and staged unfreezing is preferred over immediate end-to-end fine-tuning.

pipeline.data_validation: Load image identifiers and binary labels, verify image decoding and class support, and assign each labeled example to exactly one stratified fold before feature extraction.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: For each fold model, average original and horizontal-flip probabilities, then average those probabilities across all five fold models. No separate probability calibration is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: The method depends on access to the exact pretrained encoder and enough resources for repeated embedding extraction. Fold assignments must be created before classifier training, and no validation-fold embedding-label pair may enter that fold's classifier fit.
pipeline.feature_representation: Keep the pretrained SigLIP2 vision encoder frozen and extract 1152-dimensional image embeddings. Use horizontal flips and rotations for training views and original plus horizontal-flip views for inference.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: No single all-data refit is evidenced or required by the fold ensemble. Retain the five fold-specific classifiers and average their TTA probabilities for final test inference.
pipeline.model_stack: Train a residual multilayer classifier over frozen embeddings with hidden widths 512, 256, and 128, using batch normalization, GELU activations, dropout, residual connections, and one output logit.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Five-fold validation is evidenced. Each sample is validated by the model that excluded its fold, but persistence or aggregation of a complete OOF probability vector is not explicitly evidenced; report fold metrics without inventing an OOF aggregate.
pipeline.split_validation: Run stratified five-fold cross-validation so each fold is used once for validation and the other four folds for classifier training. Track fold ROC-AUC and early-stop each classifier independently.
pipeline.training_protocol: For each fold, optimize label-smoothed BCE with AdamW and cosine annealing, use mixed precision where supported, and retain the epoch with the best fold validation ROC-AUC.

nodes.title: Frozen SigLIP2 Features with Five-Fold Residual-MLP Ensembling
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a large pretrained vision encoder is available but repeated end-to-end fine-tuning is too expensive; sufficient storage and compute are required to extract augmented embeddings and train five classifier heads.

pipeline.data_validation: Load image identifiers and binary labels, verify that images decode successfully and both target classes are present, and inspect class counts before stratification.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No TTA, model ensemble, SWA, or explicit probability calibration is evidenced. Convert the selected model's logits directly to sigmoid probabilities.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Low resolution and training from scratch limit representation capacity and may miss subtle morphology. MixUp targets are for loss computation only; ROC-AUC must be calculated against untouched binary validation labels.
pipeline.feature_representation: Resize images to 32x32, normalize with ImageNet statistics, and apply random horizontal flip, rotation, color jitter, and MixUp during training.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: An all-data refit is not evidenced. Reload the best holdout checkpoint and run deterministic resize, normalization, and sigmoid inference on test images.
pipeline.model_stack: Train a four-layer convolutional network with channel widths 32, 64, 128, and 128, batch normalization, ReLU, max pooling, adaptive global pooling, and a dropout-regularized fully connected binary head.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single holdout. Use only the fixed 20% validation partition for model selection and performance estimation.
pipeline.split_validation: Create one stratified 80/20 train-validation split. Keep validation transforms deterministic and select the best epoch using validation ROC-AUC with patience-5 early stopping.
pipeline.training_protocol: Use BCEWithLogitsLoss, AdamW, cosine annealing, automatic mixed precision, MixUp, and early stopping based on validation ROC-AUC.

nodes.title: Compact Four-Block CNN with MixUp for Low-Resolution Training
nodes.when_to_use: Use when pretrained backbones are unavailable or GPU resources are very limited and a lightweight model trained on 32x32 images is required.

nodes.instruction: Create separate AdamW parameter groups, using 5e-5 for pretrained backbone parameters and 1e-3 for the newly initialized classifier head; combine this with warmup and cosine decay.
nodes.title: Differential Backbone and Head Learning Rates
nodes.when_to_use: Use during end-to-end transfer learning when the pretrained representation should adapt conservatively while the binary head must learn quickly.

nodes.instruction: Use interpolated labels only to compute the training loss. Preserve untouched binary labels for ROC-AUC tracking, and always calculate validation AUC on an unmixed validation loader.
nodes.title: CutMix and MixUp Target Separation for AUC Evaluation
nodes.when_to_use: Use whenever CutMix or MixUp produces continuous targets in a binary classification pipeline evaluated by ROC-AUC.

nodes.instruction: Train the replacement classifier while the pretrained backbone is frozen for five epochs, then unfreeze the backbone and continue with a reduced backbone learning rate.
nodes.title: Staged Backbone Unfreezing
nodes.when_to_use: Use when immediate end-to-end fine-tuning is unstable or when the newly initialized head needs to settle before pretrained features are adapted.

nodes.instruction: Generate probabilities for deterministic flip variants and average probabilities rather than class decisions. Use original plus horizontal flip for the two-view design, or original, horizontal, vertical, and both flips for the four-view design.
nodes.title: Deterministic Flip Test-Time Augmentation
nodes.when_to_use: Use when cactus presence should be invariant to image orientation and the extra inference cost is acceptable.

nodes.instruction: Train one classifier per stratified fold, retain each fold's independently selected checkpoint, produce TTA-averaged probabilities from every classifier, and take the arithmetic mean across the five fold models.
nodes.title: Fold-Model Probability Averaging
nodes.when_to_use: Use when five-fold training is computationally practical and lower-variance test predictions are more valuable than maintaining a single final model.

pipeline.data_validation: Verify one-to-one alignment between tabular rows and leaf images, confirm that margin, shape, and texture groups are numeric, check labels and class count, and handle non-finite engineered statistics before scaling.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No ensemble or separate calibration is evidenced. Convert logits to softmax probabilities and preserve the complete class ordering.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not fit scaling or PCA using validation or test rows. This family depends on accessible, correctly aligned images and pretrained ResNet weights; it is unsuitable when image extraction is unavailable. Monitor the train-validation loss gap because the high-capacity MLP can overfit the small multiclass dataset.
pipeline.feature_representation: For each tabular group, retain the descriptors and add per-sample statistics such as mean, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis plus DCT coefficients. Extract frozen pretrained ResNet-18 image embeddings, concatenate them with the tabular representation, fit StandardScaler on training data only, and fit PCA to retain 95% variance.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Use the best holdout-selected checkpoint, apply the training-fitted scaler and PCA to test features, extract images with the same frozen ResNet-18 preprocessing, and emit normalized softmax probabilities.
pipeline.model_stack: Train an MLP with hidden widths 1024, 512, and 256, using BatchNorm, ReLU, and dropout before the multiclass output layer.
pipeline.oof_protocol: OOF not evidenced / single holdout.
pipeline.split_validation: Create the validation partition before fitting StandardScaler or PCA and monitor multiclass log loss. The evidence supports validation-based early stopping but does not establish a multi-fold protocol.
pipeline.training_protocol: Optimize with AdamW and select the checkpoint with minimum validation log loss using early stopping. Keep the ResNet-18 extractor frozen.

nodes.title: Frozen ResNet-18 embeddings plus engineered tabular features and a regularized MLP
nodes.when_to_use: Use when leaf images and margin, shape, and texture descriptors are all available, pretrained ResNet-18 inference is affordable, and a strong single-model pipeline is preferred over end-to-end vision fine-tuning.

pipeline.data_validation: Verify image-to-row alignment, the presence and numeric type of all margin, shape, and texture descriptors, finite engineered interactions and statistics, and consistent label encoding across training and inference.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No ensemble or post-hoc calibration is evidenced. Average the two mixed-label losses during MixUp training and use softmax probabilities from the selected checkpoint at inference.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Avoid fitting engineered-feature transforms before the split. The architecture is vulnerable to overfitting on the small dataset and requires careful early stopping. Do not concatenate redundant projected features if the fused tensor already contains both modalities; keep classifier dimensions consistent with the actual fusion output.
pipeline.feature_representation: Build tabular inputs from raw group features, summary statistics, pairwise interactions, and PCA components fitted on training data only. Standardize the tabular representation. Preprocess images with the DINOv2-compatible transform and extract 1024-dimensional ViT-L/14 embeddings.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Retain the best validation checkpoint, transform test tabular data with training-fitted preprocessing, extract DINOv2 embeddings with identical image transforms, and predict normalized class probabilities.
pipeline.model_stack: Project tabular and image features through separate MLPs, fuse the projected modalities with bidirectional multi-head cross-attention, and classify the fused representation with a regularized multiclass head.
pipeline.oof_protocol: OOF not evidenced / single holdout.
pipeline.split_validation: Use a stratified train-validation split before fitting tabular scaling or PCA. Select checkpoints by multiclass validation log loss rather than training accuracy.
pipeline.training_protocol: Use mixed precision and AdamW with label smoothing and feature-level MixUp. Train in two phases: first use higher dropout and a low learning rate with cosine warmup, then fine-tune with layer-dependent learning-rate multipliers. Apply early stopping on validation log loss.

nodes.title: DINOv2 image embeddings with bidirectional cross-attention and two-phase MixUp training
nodes.when_to_use: Use when high-quality pretrained DINOv2 embeddings can be extracted and there is enough accelerator memory for 1024-dimensional image features, modality projectors, and multi-head cross-attention.

pipeline.data_validation: Detect the actual margin, shape, and texture column naming pattern, verify that each expected group is complete, align every tabular identifier to an image, confirm class labels, and enforce the target class order used for probability output.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: The supported ensemble is the arithmetic mean of probabilities from the same model family across folds. No separate post-hoc calibration is evidenced. Renormalize probabilities and retain the encoded class order.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not assume a fixed underscore convention for feature columns. Missing or misaligned images invalidate multimodal training. Attention fusion can overfit this small dataset, so retain regularization and early stopping. Never fit scaling or PCA globally before cross-validation.
pipeline.feature_representation: Keep the three 64-dimensional tabular groups separate. Extract frozen 1152-dimensional SigLIP2 image embeddings; either project the full embeddings or reduce them with training-fold PCA when memory or overfitting requires compression. Standardize tabular and image inputs with fold-fitted transforms.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: Use the fold ensemble for final inference; a separate full-data refit is not evidenced. Reuse each fold's scaler, optional PCA, SigLIP2 preprocessing, and checkpoint for its test prediction before averaging probabilities.
pipeline.model_stack: Encode margin, shape, and texture with separate MLP branches, project the SigLIP2 vector into a fourth embedding, treat the four embeddings as modality tokens, fuse them with multi-head self-attention and mean pooling, and pass the result to a dropout-regularized classifier head.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Run all stratified folds, place each fold's held-out probabilities into its corresponding OOF rows, and compute log loss once from the complete OOF matrix. Average fold-model test probabilities.
pipeline.split_validation: Use stratified folds when running the corroborated cross-validation form. Within every fold, fit StandardScaler and any dimensionality reduction only on that fold's training rows, and evaluate multiclass log loss on its held-out rows.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train each fold with AdamW, label-smoothed cross-entropy, cosine annealing, mixed precision, and early stopping on held-out log loss. Keep SigLIP2 frozen when using pre-extracted embeddings.

nodes.title: SigLIP2 multimodal token fusion with separate leaf-feature encoders
nodes.when_to_use: Use when images are available and frozen SigLIP2 extraction is feasible, while preserving separate inductive biases for margin, shape, texture, and image modalities.

pipeline.data_validation: Confirm the three 64-feature groups, encode species labels consistently, inspect missing and non-finite values, and guard ratio and interaction features against zero denominators or extreme values.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No ensemble or independent calibration is evidenced. Use the best neural checkpoint alone and obtain probabilities with softmax.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Complex statistics and cross-features can inflate dimensionality or introduce unstable values; remove or sanitize invalid interactions. Do not fit PCA or scaling before splitting. Residual depth, SE modules, MixUp, and smoothing together can underfit if regularization is too aggressive, while removing them can cause rapid overfitting.
pipeline.feature_representation: For each feature group, combine PCA retaining 95% variance with statistics including mean, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, percentiles, and range. Add evidenced cross-group ratios and product interactions, then fit RobustScaler using training rows only.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Apply the split-fitted feature pipeline to test rows and use the best early-stopped checkpoint for inference, preserving the label encoder's class order.
pipeline.model_stack: Process margin, shape, and texture through three separate branches containing three residual blocks each. Apply squeeze-excitation recalibration to branch representations, fuse the branches, and classify with a regularized multiclass head.
pipeline.oof_protocol: OOF not evidenced / single holdout.
pipeline.split_validation: Create a stratified train-validation split before fitting PCA or RobustScaler. Monitor multiclass validation log loss with early stopping patience of 10.
pipeline.training_protocol: Use MixUp, progressively annealed label smoothing, AdamW, cosine annealing, gradient clipping, mixed precision, and early stopping based on validation log loss.

nodes.title: Residual squeeze-excitation network over engineered margin, shape, and texture branches
nodes.when_to_use: Use when the 192 structured descriptors are reliable but image embeddings are unavailable or too expensive, and richer per-group interactions are needed than a flat MLP can provide.

pipeline.data_validation: Verify complete margin, shape, and texture groups, finite numeric values, valid binary leaf images, and stable extraction of contour descriptors such as Hu moments, circularity, and aspect ratio. Confirm that every class is represented in the stratification design.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Blend probabilities using fixed weights of 0.6 for LightGBM and 0.4 for logistic regression. Do not train a stacking meta-learner on the small OOF sample; normalize the weighted probabilities if necessary.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Global preprocessing before folds causes leakage. Excessive ratio, difference, and cross features can overfit, and a learned stacking layer is poorly supported for this sample size. The recipe also depends on consistently segmented images for reliable contour descriptors.
pipeline.feature_representation: For each tabular group, standardize and retain 32 PCA components, then add mean, standard deviation, maximum, minimum, median, and sum plus cross-products between feature types. Append image-derived shape descriptors and scale the combined representation within each fold.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: Use the five fold-specific preprocessing pipelines and model pairs for inference, blend each pair 0.6/0.4, and average across folds. A separate full-data refit is not evidenced.
pipeline.model_stack: Train a regularized multiclass LightGBM model with up to 1000 estimators and fold-level early stopping, alongside OneVsRest logistic regression with C equal to 0.5.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Generate held-out probabilities from both models for every one of the five folds, blend them per row, and calculate multiclass log loss from the complete blended OOF matrix. Average fold-specific blended test predictions.
pipeline.split_validation: Use 5-fold stratified cross-validation. In each fold, fit StandardScaler, 32-component PCA transformations, statistical-feature processing, and final scaling only on the fold's training rows.
pipeline.training_protocol: Use LightGBM L1/L2 regularization, including the evidenced L1 penalty and minimum child-sample control, with early stopping patience of 100. Fit logistic regression on the same fold-specific representation.

nodes.title: Leakage-safe LightGBM and logistic-regression probability blend
nodes.when_to_use: Use when compute is primarily CPU-oriented, structured descriptors and binary-image shape measurements are available, and a lower-variance classical ensemble is preferred to a high-capacity neural fusion model.

pipeline.data_validation: Verify that margin, shape, and texture each contain 64 numeric features, inspect missing and non-finite values, encode labels consistently, and ensure stratified folds retain feasible class coverage.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Use equal-weight probability averaging across fold checkpoints. No heterogeneous ensemble or post-hoc calibration is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Never standardize before fold assignment. With only three semantic feature tokens and a small dataset, a deeper or wider Transformer can overfit; retain the compact two-layer design, noise augmentation, label smoothing, and early stopping.
pipeline.feature_representation: Standardize each fold's numeric inputs using training rows only. Embed each 64-dimensional feature group with its own linear projection, prepend a learned CLS token, and treat the resulting group embeddings as Transformer tokens. Apply Gaussian noise augmentation only during training.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: Use the eight fold models and their fold-specific standardizers for final inference. A separate all-data refit is not evidenced; preserve class order and normalize the averaged probabilities.
pipeline.model_stack: Pass the CLS token and three group tokens through a two-layer Transformer encoder, then classify from the encoded CLS representation with a linear multiclass head.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Train all eight folds, store each held-out fold's probabilities in a complete OOF matrix, score that matrix with multiclass log loss, and average the eight test-probability matrices.
pipeline.split_validation: Use 8-fold stratified cross-validation. Fit standardization independently inside each fold and monitor held-out multiclass log loss with early stopping.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train with AdamW, label smoothing, warmup followed by cosine annealing, Gaussian feature noise, and early stopping on fold validation log loss.

nodes.title: Feature-group Transformer with eight-fold probability averaging
nodes.when_to_use: Use when only the structured 192-dimensional descriptors are required and the goal is to model interactions among margin, shape, and texture as a small token sequence without a vision backbone.

nodes.instruction: Create the holdout or fold assignment first; fit StandardScaler, RobustScaler, PCA, interaction processing, and other learned transformations only on the corresponding training rows, then transform validation and test rows without refitting.
nodes.title: Split-first fitting of scaling and dimensionality reduction
nodes.when_to_use: Use whenever preprocessing estimates parameters from the data, especially with the small leaf dataset where leakage can produce unrealistically low log loss.

nodes.instruction: First train projection and classifier layers with the vision representation frozen, cosine warmup, and stronger dropout; then fine-tune permitted upper vision or fusion layers using a lower learning rate for pretrained parameters, a higher learning rate for tabular and classifier parameters, MixUp, label smoothing, mixed precision, and early stopping on log loss.
nodes.title: Two-phase frozen-to-fine-tuned multimodal training
nodes.when_to_use: Use when frozen pretrained image features plateau but full-backbone training would overfit or destabilize optimization.

nodes.instruction: Preserve the three 64-feature groups through separate normalization and learned encoders, then fuse only their latent representations through concatenation, attention, or a compact Transformer.
nodes.title: Separate encoders for margin, shape, and texture
nodes.when_to_use: Use when the feature groups have different statistical behavior and a flat projection would erase their semantic structure.

nodes.instruction: Blend fold-level LightGBM and OneVsRest logistic-regression probabilities with fixed weights of 0.6 and 0.4, respectively, then average the blended test probabilities across folds.
nodes.title: Fixed probability blending instead of learned stacking
nodes.when_to_use: Use when model errors are complementary but the OOF sample is too small to support a stable stacking meta-learner.

nodes.instruction: Apply MixUp with moderate strength, evidenced at alpha 0.2, compute the weighted loss for the paired targets, and combine it with approximately 0.1 label smoothing while selecting checkpoints by validation log loss.
nodes.title: Moderate MixUp and label smoothing for small-class-per-sample regimes
nodes.when_to_use: Use when training confidence rises much faster than validation quality or when near-perfect training accuracy indicates overfitting.

pipeline.data_validation: Match noisy and clean images by image identity; load both as grayscale, normalize to [0,1], verify each pair has identical dimensions, and retain each image's actual height and width rather than assuming a common canvas size.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No multi-model ensemble or calibration is evidenced. Within each image, combine overlapping patch predictions with a Gaussian weight map.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not split after patch extraction, evaluate only isolated patches, or allocate reconstruction buffers from one assumed image size. Patch overlap and weighted blending are required to limit seams, and encoder-decoder channel and spatial dimensions must remain compatible at every skip connection.
pipeline.feature_representation: Extract overlapping 256x256 grayscale patches with stride 192 from each partition independently. Preserve patch coordinates and original dimensions for reconstruction.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Retain the checkpoint with the lowest full-image holdout RMSE, run overlapping-patch inference on every test image, Gaussian-blend the patches at their recorded coordinates, crop to the image's actual dimensions, and clip predictions to [0,1].
pipeline.model_stack: Use a four-level U-Net with 64 base channels, convolutional encoder and decoder blocks, skip connections, transposed-convolution upsampling, and a single-channel bounded output.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single 80/20 image-level holdout; do not present holdout predictions as OOF predictions.
pipeline.split_validation: Split paired images 80/20 at the image level before extracting patches so that patches from one document cannot occur in both partitions. Select checkpoints by RMSE after reconstructing complete validation images.
pipeline.training_protocol: Optimize a combined Charbonnier and L1 reconstruction loss with AdamW, warmup followed by cosine learning-rate decay, mixed-precision training, and early stopping with patience 10.

nodes.title: Four-Level Patch U-Net with Charbonnier-L1 Training and Gaussian Reconstruction
nodes.when_to_use: Use as a strong general-purpose baseline when grayscale documents have varying dimensions, GPU memory favors patch training, and preserving full image resolution is important.

pipeline.data_validation: Load paired grayscale images, normalize the raw intensity using global statistics computed only from noisy training images, verify noisy-clean dimension agreement, and record masks identifying original pixels when padding is introduced.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No model ensemble or post-hoc calibration is evidenced. Clip the single model's output to [0,1].
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not recompute normalization statistics from validation or test images, feed raw three-channel tensors to a model trained for seven channels, include padding in the objective or RMSE, or apply geometric augmentation to inputs without applying the identical transform to targets and valid masks.
pipeline.feature_representation: Construct seven channels from the noisy image: normalized intensity, median-filter response, Gaussian-blur response, Laplacian, Sobel magnitude, local standard deviation, and CLAHE. Pad or patch consistently while retaining a valid-pixel mask.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Use the best holdout checkpoint, reproduce the seven feature channels with the training-set normalization statistics, predict padded or patched test images, discard padded regions, restore original dimensions, and clip to [0,1].
pipeline.model_stack: Train a four-level U-Net taking seven input channels and producing one denoised channel, using convolution-batch-normalization-activation blocks, max-pooling, transposed-convolution decoding, and skip connections.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single 80/20 image-level holdout. No fold-wise models or complete OOF prediction set are supported.
pipeline.split_validation: Create an 80/20 image-level train-validation split before patching or augmentation. Compute validation RMSE only over original, unpadded pixels.
pipeline.training_protocol: Use masked MSE so padded pixels contribute no gradient, AdamW, cosine annealing, mixed precision with gradient scaling, and early stopping with patience 10 based on valid-region validation RMSE.

nodes.title: Seven-Channel Feature U-Net with Valid-Region MSE
nodes.when_to_use: Use when document corruption can be exposed by local edges, smoothing filters, contrast enhancement, and texture statistics, and the extra preprocessing and storage for multichannel features are affordable.

pipeline.data_validation: Pair noisy and clean grayscale images, normalize intensities to [0,1], verify dimensions per pair, and use reflection padding where patches extend beyond an image boundary.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No model ensemble or calibration is evidenced. Gaussian-weight overlapping predictions within each image during reconstruction.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Avoid using patch-level validation as the sole selection signal because it does not expose full-image seams. The compact model can underfit complex corruption, while unnecessarily increasing decoder depth or adding unstable frequency-domain objectives can degrade training.
pipeline.feature_representation: Extract overlapping 256x64 patches with stride 64. Stack grayscale into three channels for the evidenced implementation and apply the corresponding fixed channel normalization consistently.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A refit on all paired images is not evidenced. Apply the lowest-RMSE holdout checkpoint to overlapping test patches, reconstruct with Gaussian weights, remove reflection padding, restore each original image extent, and clip to [0,1].
pipeline.model_stack: Use a compact encoder-decoder beginning with a learnable 3x3 stochastic filtering convolution, followed by residual encoder stages with 32, 64, and 128 channels, stride-2 downsampling, bilinear decoder upsampling, skip connections, and a sigmoid output.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single 80/20 image-level holdout; there is no supported cross-validation or OOF aggregation.
pipeline.split_validation: Split images 80/20 before patch extraction. During model selection, reconstruct each held-out image and compute per-image full-resolution RMSE rather than relying only on patch RMSE.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train with Charbonnier loss, AdamW, cosine annealing with warm restarts, mixed precision, and early stopping with patience 15.

nodes.title: Lightweight Residual Encoder-Decoder with Stochastic Front-End
nodes.when_to_use: Use when the dataset is small enough that a large U-Net risks overfitting, but a compact model with local filtering, residual feature extraction, and patch overlap fits available compute.

pipeline.data_validation: Load aligned noisy-clean grayscale pairs in [0,1], verify matching dimensions, retain image identifiers and patch coordinates, and ensure every pixel is covered by at least one extracted patch.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No multi-checkpoint ensemble or calibration is evidenced. Average overlapping patch outputs with spatial weights during image reconstruction.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not infer with non-overlapping tiles when boundary artifacts matter. Aggressive augmentation or structurally complex losses can introduce numerical instability; gradient clipping and a stable pixel loss are important. Patch extraction must preserve enough overlap to reconstruct every pixel.
pipeline.feature_representation: Use single-channel overlapping patches, evidenced at 256x64 with stride 64 or 256x256 with stride 64-128. Apply paired horizontal flips and small rotations only to training input-target patches.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Load the checkpoint with minimum reconstructed-image validation RMSE, infer all overlapping test patches, weighted-average them into the original image geometry, and clamp the final pixels to [0,1].
pipeline.model_stack: Use NAFNet with width 32, encoder and decoder stages built from nonlinear-activation-free blocks, instance normalization, SimpleGate operations, simplified channel attention, skip connections, and a deep middle stage.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single held-out image set. No fold count, OOF prediction matrix, or fold ensemble is supported.
pipeline.split_validation: Reserve complete images for validation before generating patches. The exact split ratio is not evidenced; select the checkpoint using RMSE from weighted reconstruction of the held-out full images.
pipeline.training_protocol: Optimize MSE with AdamW, mixed precision, gradient clipping, and early stopping with patience 5. Dense overlap increases the effective training sample count and weighted reconstruction is used for validation.

nodes.title: NAFNet Patch Denoiser with Weighted Full-Image Validation
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a restoration-specific architecture is preferred over a conventional U-Net and compute supports a width-32 encoder-decoder with multiple activation-free middle blocks.

pipeline.data_validation: Load paired grayscale images in [0,1], confirm that noisy and clean dimensions agree, and preserve original dimensions plus patch coordinates for full-image reconstruction.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No model ensemble or calibration is evidenced. Use weighted overlap averaging as the only aggregation mechanism.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Attention adds capacity and is not a substitute for leakage-safe splitting or adequate patch diversity. Do not augment validation data, split patches from the same image across partitions, or evaluate RMSE on padded or uncovered regions.
pipeline.feature_representation: Use raw grayscale patches and apply paired horizontal flips, random 90-degree rotations, and brightness-contrast adjustments to training samples only.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: No full-data refit is evidenced. Run the best holdout checkpoint over overlapping test patches, weighted-average outputs into each full image, restore exact original dimensions, and clip values to [0,1].
pipeline.model_stack: Use a U-Net with double-convolution encoder-decoder blocks, max-pooling, bilinear upsampling, skip connections, and squeeze-and-excitation blocks at each stage to recalibrate channels.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single image-level holdout; no robust OOF or cross-validation procedure is supported.
pipeline.split_validation: Perform an image-level train-validation split before extracting 128x128 patches with stride 64. Reconstruct held-out images by weighted averaging and minimize full-image RMSE.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train with MSE, AdamW, mixed precision, and early stopping with patience 5. Keep validation transformations deterministic and retain the checkpoint with the lowest reconstructed-image RMSE.

nodes.title: SE-Attention U-Net with Dense Patch Augmentation
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a standard U-Net is stable but needs stronger channel selection for separating text structure from document noise, and enough overlapping patches can be generated to regularize the added attention capacity.

nodes.instruction: Assign complete noisy-clean image pairs to training or validation first, then extract patches independently. Select models using RMSE after reconstructing complete validation images rather than treating correlated patches as independent validation examples.
nodes.title: Split Documents Before Patch Generation
nodes.when_to_use: Use for every patch-based denoising pipeline, especially when neighboring patches overlap heavily.

nodes.instruction: Infer overlapping patches, multiply each prediction by a Gaussian spatial weight that downweights patch borders, accumulate weighted predictions and weights at their original coordinates, and divide the two accumulators pixelwise.
nodes.title: Gaussian-Weighted Overlap Reconstruction
nodes.when_to_use: Use when tiled inference produces seams or patch-border errors and stride is smaller than patch size.

nodes.instruction: Carry a valid-pixel mask through preprocessing and augmentation; multiply squared error by that mask and normalize by the valid-pixel count. Apply the same exclusion when computing validation RMSE and crop predictions to original dimensions.
nodes.title: Mask Padding Out of Loss and RMSE
nodes.when_to_use: Use whenever variable-sized images are padded to a shared canvas or model-compatible multiple.

nodes.instruction: Apply the same random flip, rotation, and translation to each noisy patch, clean target, engineered feature stack, and validity mask. Keep validation deterministic; use denser patch overlap when the number of source images is small.
nodes.title: Paired Geometric Augmentation for Scarce Documents
nodes.when_to_use: Use when training loss improves while held-out full-image RMSE plateaus, indicating limited effective sample diversity.

nodes.instruction: Recalibrate intermediate channels with squeeze-and-excitation blocks in U-Net stages or simplified channel attention inside NAF blocks, while retaining encoder-decoder skip connections for spatial detail.
nodes.title: Channel Attention at Restoration Stages
nodes.when_to_use: Use when the baseline has adequate spatial capacity but struggles to distinguish text strokes and useful local structure from corruption.

pipeline.data_validation: Parse pickup timestamps; drop training rows with missing coordinates; restrict pickup and dropoff coordinates to plausible NYC bounds; remove invalid fare targets and implausible passenger counts; verify engineered numeric features are finite.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No ensemble or separate calibration is evidenced. Use the single best-iteration LightGBM prediction.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not fit scalers or other learned transforms on validation or inference data. Do not treat implausible training coordinates, fares, or passenger counts as valid observations. Ensure temporal and spatial feature definitions are identical between training and inference.
pipeline.feature_representation: Extract year, month, day, hour, day of week, and weekend indicators. Add haversine and Manhattan distances, bearing, distances to airports, grid-cell or location indicators, a Manhattan indicator, and interactions such as hour-by-distance, weekend-by-distance, and Manhattan-ride flags. Standardize numeric features using statistics fitted on the training partition only.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Apply the same fitted feature transforms to every inference row and predict with the validation-selected LightGBM iteration.
pipeline.model_stack: Train one regularized LightGBM regressor with an RMSE regression objective, approximately 2000 boosting rounds available, and L1/L2 regularization such as reg_alpha=5 and reg_lambda=10.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced; this is a single temporal holdout and does not produce OOF predictions.
pipeline.split_validation: Sort by pickup time and reserve the latest 5% as a temporal validation set; evaluate with RMSE and use the split only for model selection and early stopping.
pipeline.training_protocol: Fit on the temporal training partition with validation RMSE monitoring and early stopping after 100 rounds without improvement; retain the iteration with the lowest validation RMSE.

nodes.title: Large-scale temporally validated LightGBM with rich spatial interactions
nodes.when_to_use: Use when tens of millions of training rows are available, CPU and memory resources can support large-scale gradient boosting, and validation should reflect temporal drift.

pipeline.data_validation: Remove rows with missing coordinates, restrict coordinates to plausible NYC bounds, and reject invalid fare targets and passenger counts before constructing target strata.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No ensemble or probability-style calibration is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Fare bins are validation-design artifacts and must not be model inputs. Fit any learned preprocessing only on the training partition. This random stratified design does not test chronological generalization and should not be interpreted as a temporal backtest.
pipeline.feature_representation: Extract calendar and clock features including hour, day, month, rush-hour and night flags, plus cyclical hour sine/cosine terms. Add haversine distance, Manhattan distance, bearing, airport and Manhattan-center distances, log-transformed distance, coordinate interactions, and NYC location flags.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit after early stopping is not evidenced. Transform inference data with the same deterministic feature functions and generate fares with the best validation iteration.
pipeline.model_stack: Train a single tuned LightGBM regression model on the raw fare target with up to 2000 boosting rounds.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced; this design uses one fare-stratified 80/20 holdout rather than full cross-validation.
pipeline.split_validation: Bin fare_amount and create an 80/20 train-validation split stratified by those fare bins. Report RMSE on the untouched validation partition and use it for early stopping.
pipeline.training_protocol: Monitor validation RMSE and stop after 50 rounds without improvement; retain the best-scoring iteration.

nodes.title: Fare-stratified LightGBM with cyclical time and landmark features
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a representative random holdout is acceptable and the heavy-tailed fare distribution makes ordinary random splitting prone to uneven target coverage.

pipeline.data_validation: Filter invalid training coordinates, fares, and passenger counts; validate timestamps; and ensure all distance and cluster inputs are finite before fitting the model.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No ensemble or post-hoc calibration is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not scale integer zone IDs as continuous numeric features when they are modeled categorically. Coarse or unstable clusters can erase local fare structure, while excessive cluster counts can create sparse zone pairs. Cluster fitting must not use fare targets.
pipeline.feature_representation: Create hour, weekday, holiday, rush-hour, and cyclical time features; haversine and Manhattan distances; airport and city-center distances; and pickup/dropoff zone IDs from MiniBatchKMeans with approximately 100 geographic clusters. Add a pickup-zone/dropoff-zone pair interaction.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Reuse the fitted zone model and deterministic feature pipeline, then infer with the best early-stopped LightGBM iteration.
pipeline.model_stack: Train a single LightGBM regressor with RMSE objective, max_depth around 8, num_leaves around 64, and as many as 5000 boosting rounds.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced; this is a single chronological 80/20 holdout.
pipeline.split_validation: Sort by pickup time and use the first 80% for training and the latest 20% for validation. Select the model by validation RMSE.
pipeline.training_protocol: Fit clustering from training locations rather than validation targets, transform validation and inference coordinates with the fitted clusterer, and train LightGBM with validation-based early stopping.

nodes.title: Zone-pair LightGBM with fine-grained NYC location clusters
nodes.when_to_use: Use when pickup and dropoff coordinates are plentiful enough to learn stable geographic zones and additional clustering cost is acceptable.

pipeline.data_validation: Restrict coordinates to plausible NYC bounds, keep positive fares below the evidenced upper bound, and retain only reasonable passenger counts. Confirm that fares are positive before applying log1p.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Average raw-scale predictions from the two models and clip the final fare prediction to the evidenced range of 1 to 100. Validate the blend against each component before adopting it.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Never average a log-scale prediction directly with a dollar-scale prediction. The observed blend did not improve the referenced baseline, so retain it only if the shared holdout confirms a lower RMSE. Clipping bounds can bias unusually expensive rides.
pipeline.feature_representation: Use common temporal features, rush-hour flags, cyclical encodings, haversine and Manhattan distances, bearing, airport and Manhattan distances, and related spatial interactions for both component models.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Apply both best-iteration models to the identically engineered inference matrix, invert the log-target prediction, average on the fare scale, and clip.
pipeline.model_stack: Train two LightGBM regressors: one directly on fare_amount and one on log1p(fare_amount). Convert log-model predictions back with expm1 and average them with raw-target predictions.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced; blending weights are assessed on a single shared holdout, not on OOF predictions.
pipeline.split_validation: Use the established validation partition from the base LightGBM pipeline and evaluate each component and the blend by RMSE on exactly the same rows. The evidence does not establish cross-validation.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train both models independently with early stopping on the same validation split and retain each model's best iteration.

nodes.title: Raw-target and log-target LightGBM blend for skewed fares
nodes.when_to_use: Use when fares are strongly right-skewed and resources permit training two complementary boosting models on the same engineered table.

pipeline.data_validation: While reading training data in chunks, remove invalid coordinates, fare outliers, and implausible passenger counts. Parse timestamps and verify that engineered continuous features contain no unresolved missing or infinite values.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: No ensemble or separate calibration is evidenced. Use the best validation checkpoint from the selected loss configuration.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Fit normalization only on the training partition. Run validation and inference in batches to control memory use. Huber loss is not automatically superior here—the evidenced Huber variant had worse RMSE—so select the loss by held-out RMSE rather than robustness claims alone.
pipeline.feature_representation: Use standardized continuous inputs derived from year, month, day, hour, day of week, weekend, haversine distance, bearing, and distances to JFK, LGA, and EWR.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data neural-network refit is not evidenced. Reuse training-partition normalization statistics and the best checkpoint for batched inference.
pipeline.model_stack: Use a three-hidden-layer MLP with widths 256, 256, and 128, BatchNorm, ReLU activations, and dropout, followed by a scalar fare output.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced; the deterministic hash assignment provides one holdout and no OOF prediction matrix.
pipeline.split_validation: Assign rows deterministically to a 90/10 train-validation split using a stable key hash. Keep the hash rule fixed across chunks and evaluate the held-out partition with RMSE.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train with AdamW and either MSE loss or Huber loss, monitor validation RMSE, apply gradient clipping for the Huber variant, and stop after two validation checks without improvement. Preserve the parameters from the lowest validation RMSE.

nodes.title: Deterministic-split regularized MLP for chunked taxi training
nodes.when_to_use: Use when training data must be processed in chunks, GPU or efficient neural-network compute is available, and a deterministic row-stable holdout is preferred.

pipeline.data_validation: Filter invalid training coordinates, fare values, distances, and passenger counts; parse temporal fields; and check that continuous and grid-derived features are finite.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Use the evidenced fixed weighted average of 0.3 neural-network prediction and 0.7 XGBoost prediction, then clip fares to the evidenced range of 1 to 500. Compare the blend with both components on the holdout.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not process a very large validation or inference matrix in one neural forward pass. Grid IDs must use the same mapping at inference. The fixed blend is justified only when it beats both components on the common temporal holdout.
pipeline.feature_representation: Create hour, day, weekday, rush-hour, haversine distance, Manhattan distance, bearing, distances to JFK, LGA, and Manhattan, and coordinate grid-cell encodings. Fit RobustScaler on training continuous features only; feed grid cells through learned geographic embeddings in the neural component.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: A full-data refit is not evidenced. Apply the training-fitted scaler and grid mapping, predict in batches with the best neural checkpoint, predict with the best XGBoost iteration, blend, and clip.
pipeline.model_stack: Train a GeoAwareNN with geographic embeddings, batch normalization, dropout, Huber loss, AdamW, and learning-rate scheduling. Train a tuned XGBoost regressor with early stopping on the same feature domain. Blend predictions with weights 0.3 for the neural network and 0.7 for XGBoost.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced; this is a single temporal holdout and the blend is not based on OOF predictions.
pipeline.split_validation: Sort observations chronologically and reserve the latest 20% for validation. Use the same validation rows to evaluate the neural network, XGBoost model, and final weighted blend by RMSE.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train both components against the shared temporal holdout; batch neural training and validation; retain the best neural checkpoint and best XGBoost iteration before blending.

nodes.title: Geo-aware neural network and XGBoost weighted hybrid
nodes.when_to_use: Use when both neural and tree-model training resources are available and complementary geographic embeddings and boosted-tree interactions justify the added complexity.

nodes.instruction: Create the validation split before fitting StandardScaler, RobustScaler, clustering, imputation statistics, or target-derived group statistics. Fit each transform on training rows and only transform validation and inference rows.
nodes.title: Fit learned preprocessing strictly inside the training partition
nodes.when_to_use: Use whenever the representation contains learned preprocessing rather than purely deterministic row-wise features.

nodes.instruction: Keep pickup zone, dropoff zone, season, and similar IDs as integer categorical features; exclude them from numeric scaling and pass their categorical identities consistently to LightGBM.
nodes.title: Preserve categorical identity for geographic zones
nodes.when_to_use: Use when KMeans or grid assignments are intended as nominal location categories rather than ordered continuous measurements.

nodes.instruction: Represent each trip with haversine and Manhattan distance, direction or bearing, coordinate deltas where available, and distances to JFK, LGA, EWR, or Manhattan; combine these with hour, weekday, weekend, and rush-hour context.
nodes.title: Combine continuous trip geometry with landmark context
nodes.when_to_use: Use for NYC fare models that need both route length and location-specific surcharge or traffic context.

nodes.instruction: Set a generous boosting-round ceiling, monitor validation RMSE, stop after roughly 50 to 100 non-improving rounds, and use the best iteration for validation and inference.
nodes.title: Use early stopping as the boosting-capacity selector
nodes.when_to_use: Use when the optimal number of trees is unknown and a clean holdout is available.

nodes.instruction: Train one model on fare_amount and another on log1p(fare_amount); apply expm1 to the second model's predictions before averaging, and accept the blend only if shared-holdout RMSE improves.
nodes.title: Blend raw-target and log-target regressors only on the fare scale
nodes.when_to_use: Use when fare skew suggests complementary error behavior between absolute-error-scale and relative-error-scale models.

nodes.instruction: Evaluate validation and inference rows through bounded-size batches, accumulate squared errors across batches for RMSE, and avoid materializing a full multi-million-row neural forward pass.
nodes.title: Batch neural validation and inference
nodes.when_to_use: Use when the validation or inference matrix is too large for available accelerator or host memory.

pipeline.data_validation: Load labeled training text and unlabeled test text, verify that every training row has text and one of the three author labels, and preserve a fixed mapping between the three labels and probability columns.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: The three transformer representations are fused by feature concatenation rather than probability averaging. Additional probability ensembling or post-hoc calibration is not evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: This recipe does not fine-tune the language models, so performance is bounded by frozen CLS representations. Keep tokenizer/model pairings consistent, maintain identical feature concatenation order between training and inference, and do not describe the feature concatenation as an OOF ensemble.
pipeline.feature_representation: Tokenize each text to a maximum length of 256 with DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, and DistilBERT-base-uncased; extract each frozen model's CLS embedding and concatenate the three vectors into a 2304-dimensional representation.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: After selecting the boosting configuration from cross-validation, retrain one XGBoost model on all labeled embeddings and predict three-class probabilities for test embeddings.
pipeline.model_stack: Train an XGBoost multiclass classifier with objective multi:softprob and three output classes on the concatenated frozen embeddings.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Use the held-out portion of each of the five stratified folds for fold-level log-loss evaluation; a consolidated stored OOF prediction matrix is not evidenced.
pipeline.split_validation: Use stratified 5-fold cross-validation so every fold preserves the three-author class distribution; monitor multiclass log loss and use early stopping within each fold.
pipeline.training_protocol: Keep all transformer parameters frozen, precompute embeddings, and train each fold's XGBoost model with validation-based early stopping under multiclass log loss.

nodes.title: Frozen Multi-Transformer Embeddings with Five-Fold XGBoost
nodes.when_to_use: Use when several pretrained transformer backbones are available for batched feature extraction but end-to-end fine-tuning is undesirable or too costly; requires enough memory or storage for 2304-dimensional dense features and CPU/GPU resources for XGBoost.

pipeline.data_validation: Load raw texts, encode the three author labels consistently, verify that train and validation indices do not overlap, and retain the same label-to-probability-column mapping for inference.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Use EMA parameter averaging as the sole averaging policy. A multi-model ensemble and separate probability calibration are not evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: The single holdout can have higher variance than full cross-validation. Full-backbone large-model training is memory intensive, and the evidence supports raw-text fine-tuning rather than handcrafted-feature fusion or pseudo-labeling.
pipeline.feature_representation: Apply minimal preprocessing and tokenize raw text directly with the DeBERTa tokenizer; do not append handcrafted stylistic features.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: Restore or apply the EMA-averaged parameters and generate normalized three-class probabilities for the test texts. An additional refit on all labeled rows is not evidenced.
pipeline.model_stack: Use HuggingFace AutoModelForSequenceClassification with a DeBERTa-v3-large backbone, three output classes, and all backbone layers unfrozen.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single holdout. Report validation log loss only on the fixed stratified 10% validation partition; do not claim OOF estimates.
pipeline.split_validation: Create a stratified 90/10 train-validation split and select checkpoints by validation multiclass log loss with early stopping patience of 3.
pipeline.training_protocol: Optimize with AdamW and OneCycleLR, use mixed-precision training, clip gradients, and maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters throughout fine-tuning.

nodes.title: End-to-End DeBERTa-v3-Large Fine-Tuning with EMA Inference
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a GPU can support full DeBERTa-v3-large fine-tuning and the goal is a strong raw-text model without handcrafted features; suitable when a single stratified holdout is acceptable.

pipeline.data_validation: Load raw training and test text, encode the three author labels, verify that each stratified fold contains all classes, and keep the author-to-class index mapping fixed through inference.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Average the five fold models' test probability vectors. No additional calibration is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Processing only the first nominal fold is not this recipe; all five folds are required for its ensemble policy. Token masking must be respected during mean pooling, and fold-specific early stopping must not use test predictions.
pipeline.feature_representation: Tokenize raw text with the DeBERTa-v3 tokenizer to a maximum length of 384 and mean-pool the final hidden states using the valid-token mask.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: Retain the best checkpoint from each fold, infer on the test set with every checkpoint, average probabilities across all five folds, and preserve normalized three-class rows. A separate all-data refit is not evidenced.
pipeline.model_stack: Fine-tune DeBERTa-v3-base with a single linear three-class classifier on the mean-pooled representation.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Generate validation probabilities from the model that did not train on each fold's rows and combine the five held-out partitions for cross-validated log-loss assessment; do not train a separate stacker unless new evidence supports it.
pipeline.split_validation: Run all five folds of StratifiedKFold. Evaluate each held-out fold with multiclass log loss and use early stopping with patience of 4.
pipeline.training_protocol: Use cross-entropy with label smoothing, AdamW, linear warmup followed by ReduceLROnPlateau, mixed precision, gradient clipping, and validation-based early stopping.

nodes.title: Five-Fold Mean-Pooled DeBERTa-v3-Base Probability Ensemble
nodes.when_to_use: Use when robust cross-validated inference is preferred and compute permits five DeBERTa-v3-base fine-tuning runs; the base backbone and simple head offer a balance between capacity and implementation complexity.

pipeline.data_validation: Load passages and labels, encode EAP, HPL, and MWS consistently, verify that each row has usable text, and preserve the class order used by the probability outputs.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Average test probabilities across the three fold models. No separate calibration stage is evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Do not add mixup, TF-IDF fusion, or SWA to this recipe because they are outside the supporting execution. Large-backbone training can still overfit or exceed memory limits, so early stopping and the stated accumulation strategy are material parts of the method.
pipeline.feature_representation: Tokenize raw text directly with ModernBERT to a maximum length of 256; apply no additional feature engineering.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: Use the best checkpoint from each fold for test inference, average the three probability vectors row-wise, and keep outputs as normalized three-class probabilities. No separate all-data refit is evidenced.
pipeline.model_stack: Fine-tune ModernBERT-large with a three-class sequence-classification head.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Use each fold model to predict its held-out partition for cross-validated log-loss evaluation; the evidence supports fold validation and test averaging but does not evidence a downstream OOF stacker.
pipeline.split_validation: Use 3-fold stratified cross-validation and monitor multiclass log loss independently on each held-out fold with early stopping.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train with label-smoothed cross-entropy, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay with warmup, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, gradient clipping, and early stopping.

nodes.title: Three-Fold Raw-Text ModernBERT-Large Ensemble
nodes.when_to_use: Use when long-context ModernBERT-large fine-tuning is available and a three-model cross-validation ensemble is affordable, while avoiding handcrafted feature pipelines.

pipeline.data_validation: Load labeled and unlabeled text, encode the three authors consistently, verify that handcrafted feature extraction returns finite values for every row, and maintain identical feature definitions and class order at inference.
pipeline.ensemble_calibration: Average the RoBERTa probability output and the LightGBM one-vs-rest output. No learned blend weights or separate calibration model are evidenced.
pipeline.failure_boundaries: Because cross-fitted embeddings are not evidenced, this should not be represented as leakage-safe OOF stacking. Feature extraction must be identical between training and test data, and the one-vs-rest outputs must be placed in the fixed author order before averaging.
pipeline.feature_representation: Extract stylometric statistics including punctuation ratios, lexical diversity, readability measures, and POS/suffix approximations; also construct character and word TF-IDF n-grams plus punctuation-sequence features, and obtain RoBERTa-base contextual embeddings.
pipeline.final_refit_inference: Use the selected RoBERTa checkpoint to produce test probabilities and embeddings, apply the trained LightGBM models to the matching contextual-plus-handcrafted test representation, and average the two probability outputs. A separate all-data refit of both stages is not evidenced.
pipeline.model_stack: Fine-tune RoBERTa-base with a simple MLP classification head, then train one-vs-rest LightGBM classifiers on the concatenation of RoBERTa embeddings and handcrafted features.
pipeline.oof_protocol: Not evidenced / single holdout. The LightGBM stage is validated on the stratified holdout; cross-fitted transformer embeddings and a full OOF stacking matrix are not evidenced.
pipeline.split_validation: Create a stratified train-validation split and evaluate both the transformer and hybrid predictions with multiclass log loss; use early stopping with patience of 7 for RoBERTa training.
pipeline.training_protocol: Train RoBERTa with label-smoothed cross-entropy, AdamW, cosine learning-rate scheduling, gradient accumulation, mixed precision, and validation-based early stopping; train the LightGBM meta-classifier after extracting transformer embeddings.

nodes.title: RoBERTa Embedding and Stylometric LightGBM Hybrid
nodes.when_to_use: Use when contextual transformer signals and explicit author-style statistics are both desired and a two-stage neural-plus-tree pipeline is operationally acceptable; suitable for a single stratified holdout experiment.

nodes.instruction: Tokenize each passage to length 256 with DeBERTa-v3-base, RoBERTa-base, and DistilBERT-base-uncased, extract their frozen CLS vectors in a fixed order, and concatenate them into a 2304-dimensional feature vector for a downstream multiclass booster.
nodes.title: Concatenate Frozen CLS Embeddings from Complementary Backbones
nodes.when_to_use: Use when end-to-end fine-tuning is unavailable but several pretrained backbones can be run once for deterministic feature extraction.

nodes.instruction: Maintain an exponential moving average of all fine-tuned model parameters during training and apply the averaged parameters for validation checkpoint selection and final probability inference.
nodes.title: EMA-Averaged Transformer Parameters for Inference
nodes.when_to_use: Use during fully unfrozen transformer fine-tuning when parameter averaging is affordable and validation log loss is sensitive to noisy late updates.

nodes.instruction: Mean-pool final-layer token representations over valid, non-padding positions and feed the resulting vector directly to a single linear three-class classifier; pair it with label-smoothed cross-entropy.
nodes.title: Masked Mean Pooling with a Simple DeBERTa Head
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a stable, low-complexity alternative to custom attention pooling or deep classification heads is preferred.

nodes.instruction: Select the best checkpoint independently within every stratified fold, predict the test texts with each selected checkpoint, and take the row-wise arithmetic mean of the fold probability vectors.
nodes.title: Fold-Checkpoint Probability Averaging
nodes.when_to_use: Use only when every advertised fold has actually been trained and the compute budget supports repeated inference.

nodes.instruction: Concatenate RoBERTa contextual embeddings with punctuation, lexical-diversity, readability, POS/suffix, TF-IDF n-gram, and punctuation-sequence features; train one-vs-rest LightGBM models on the fused vectors and average their probabilities with the RoBERTa classifier probabilities.
nodes.title: Contextual-Embedding and Stylometric Tree Fusion
nodes.when_to_use: Use when explicit author-style features may add complementary information and the extra feature extraction and second-stage model are acceptable.

failure_signature.pattern: Binary ROC-AUC computation fails with "continuous format is not supported" after MixUp or CutMix produces fractional training targets.
failure_signature.root_cause: MixUp and CutMix create soft labels for loss computation, but binary ROC-AUC requires ground-truth targets from the discrete classes.

steps: Retain the original binary labels before applying MixUp or CutMix.
Use the mixed soft labels only when computing the training loss.
Compute training ROC-AUC against original binary labels, or omit training AUC for mixed batches.
Continue computing validation ROC-AUC on an augmentation-free loader with untouched binary labels.
repair_action.summary: Retain the original binary labels before applying MixUp or CutMix.

nodes.title: Preserve binary targets separately from MixUp/CutMix loss targets
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a binary image classifier applies label-mixing augmentation and metric evaluation receives fractional targets or raises a continuous-target error.

failure_signature.pattern: Binary classifier initialization fails because BCEWithLogitsLoss rejects a label_smoothing keyword.
failure_signature.root_cause: The binary BCE-with-logits loss API in the installed PyTorch version does not implement the label_smoothing option used by the pipeline.

steps: Initialize BCEWithLogitsLoss only with arguments supported by the installed runtime, preserving any required class weighting such as pos_weight.
If smoothing is necessary, transform binary targets before loss evaluation using y_smooth = y * (1 - epsilon) + 0.5 * epsilon.
Keep original unsmoothed binary targets for ROC-AUC and other classification metrics.
Otherwise remove label smoothing and use ordinary BCEWithLogitsLoss.
repair_action.summary: Initialize BCEWithLogitsLoss only with arguments supported by the installed runtime, preserving any required class weighting such as pos_weight.

nodes.title: Implement binary label smoothing outside BCEWithLogitsLoss
nodes.when_to_use: Use when training a binary image classifier and BCEWithLogitsLoss raises an unexpected-keyword TypeError for label_smoothing.

failure_signature.pattern: A shared feature-extraction routine fails on test data by unpacking the wrong number of batch fields or treating image identifiers as tensor labels.
failure_signature.root_cause: Training and validation datasets emit image-label-ID batches while the unlabeled test dataset emits image-ID batches, but the extraction routine assumes one fixed schema.

steps: Define explicit dataset contracts for labeled batches such as (images, labels, ids) and unlabeled batches such as (images, ids).
Pass an explicit labeled or unlabeled mode to the extraction routine, or branch on a validated batch schema.
Convert labels to arrays only for labeled batches and collect identifiers as strings for both schemas.
Return a consistent result structure with features, optional labels, and ordered identifiers.
Assert that extracted feature rows, optional label rows, and identifier counts agree before caching or inference.
repair_action.summary: Define explicit dataset contracts for labeled batches such as (images, labels, ids) and unlabeled batches such as (images, ids).

nodes.title: Normalize labeled and unlabeled DataLoader batch schemas during feature extraction
nodes.when_to_use: Use when one frozen vision feature extractor serves train, validation, and unlabeled test loaders whose dataset outputs have different tuple structures.

failure_signature.pattern: Cross-validation ensemble inference completes, but submission creation fails because the number or order of test identifiers does not match the averaged test predictions.
failure_signature.root_cause: Test identifiers are incompletely accumulated, overwritten between batches or folds, or collected independently from the prediction order.

steps: Use a deterministic test loader with shuffling disabled.
During one complete inference pass, append every batch's identifiers to a flat ordered list alongside its prediction vector.
For later folds, reuse the established identifier order and verify that each fold emits the same ordered identifiers.
Average fold predictions only after asserting identical prediction shapes across folds.
Before creating the submission, assert that identifier count equals prediction count and equals the test dataset size.
repair_action.summary: Use a deterministic test loader with shuffling disabled.

nodes.title: Build submission identifiers from the same ordered inference stream as predictions
nodes.when_to_use: Use when producing an ensemble submission and test IDs are gathered inside batch or fold loops, especially after a length mismatch at DataFrame construction.

failure_signature.pattern: A custom CNN reaches its classifier but fails matrix multiplication because flattened convolutional features do not match the first linear layer's declared input width.
failure_signature.root_cause: The classifier input dimension was calculated from an incorrect channel count or spatial resolution after pooling.

steps: Run a representative image tensor through the convolutional feature stack before training and inspect the resulting shape.
Set the first linear layer's input width to the product of the actual non-batch feature dimensions.
Prefer adaptive pooling to a fixed spatial size when input resolution or convolutional geometry may vary.
Add a model smoke test that performs one forward pass and asserts an output shape of one logit per image.
repair_action.summary: Run a representative image tensor through the convolutional feature stack before training and inspect the resulting shape.

nodes.title: Derive CNN classifier input width from the actual feature tensor
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a from-scratch CNN for fixed-size cactus images reports incompatible matrix shapes at the convolutional-to-linear boundary.

failure_signature.pattern: Training and checkpoint saving succeed, but loading the best checkpoint for test inference raises a weights-only unpickling error under newer PyTorch behavior.
