failure_signature.root_cause: The pipeline saves a general Python checkpoint object while loading it through a runtime whose torch.load defaults to restricted weights-only deserialization.

steps: Save the model state_dict and primitive metadata instead of serializing the complete model object.
Recreate the model architecture in code before loading the checkpoint.
Load the state dictionary with the runtime's explicit weights-only mode and then call model.load_state_dict.
Use unrestricted deserialization only for a trusted legacy checkpoint that cannot be converted, and specify that behavior explicitly.
Perform a checkpoint reload smoke test immediately after saving, before the full training run proceeds to final inference.
repair_action.summary: Save the model state_dict and primitive metadata instead of serializing the complete model object.

nodes.title: Save and reload model state dictionaries with an explicit checkpoint contract
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a best-model checkpoint saved during binary image training cannot be reloaded because of PyTorch weights-only deserialization behavior.

failure_signature.pattern: A multimodal forward pass concatenates or selects projected tabular, image, gated, or cross-attended tensors whose total width differs from the first classifier linear layer, causing a matrix-multiplication shape mismatch.
failure_signature.root_cause: The fusion representation was changed without updating the classifier contract, or modality projections already represented inside a fused tensor were concatenated again.

steps: Write down the output width of every tabular projection, image projection, attention output, and fused representation.
Choose one explicit final representation and remove redundant modality tensors that are already encoded in it.
Set the classifier's first linear layer input width from the chosen representation's computed dimension rather than a stale constant.
Run a representative batch through the forward pass and assert that final_features.shape[-1] equals classifier[0].in_features before training.
repair_action.summary: Write down the output width of every tabular projection, image projection, attention output, and fused representation.

nodes.title: derive multimodal classifier input width from the actual fusion output
nodes.when_to_use: Use when multimodal model_forward fails with incompatible mat1 and mat2 dimensions and the observed final feature width differs from the classifier's declared input width.

failure_signature.pattern: The backward pass fails with 'grad can be implicitly created only for scalar outputs' after MixUp or CutMix combines unreduced per-sample classification losses.
failure_signature.root_cause: The augmentation criterion preserves the batch dimension because its component loss uses no reduction, and the weighted combination is passed directly to backward.

steps: Compute the loss for each augmented target using the same per-sample reduction.
Combine the two loss tensors with the MixUp or CutMix coefficient.
Apply an explicit mean reduction to the combined loss before backward.
Assert that loss.ndim is zero in the training loop, including augmented and non-augmented branches.
repair_action.summary: Compute the loss for each augmented target using the same per-sample reduction.

nodes.title: reduce augmented per-sample losses to a scalar before backpropagation
nodes.when_to_use: Use when MixUp or CutMix training reaches the backward pass with a vector-valued loss and raises the scalar-output gradient error.

failure_signature.pattern: SMOTE fails inside a stratified training fold because its requested nearest-neighbor count, including the sample itself, exceeds the number of examples in at least one class.
failure_signature.root_cause: A fixed k_neighbors value was selected from the full-dataset expectation even though the 99-class training fold contains classes with fewer than k_neighbors plus one samples.

steps: Count samples per class after creating the training fold and before applying SMOTE.
Set k_neighbors no larger than the minimum supported value, specifically at most min_class_count minus one.
Skip SMOTE or use a non-neighbor-based resampling method if any training-fold class has fewer than two samples.
Fit and apply resampling only to the training fold; leave validation and test distributions unchanged.
repair_action.summary: Count samples per class after creating the training fold and before applying SMOTE.

nodes.title: configure SMOTE neighbors from the smallest training-fold class
nodes.when_to_use: Use when SMOTE reports that n_neighbors is greater than n_samples_fit for a minority class in a leaf-classification training fold.

failure_signature.pattern: Loading a validated model checkpoint into the full-data retraining model fails because the checkpoint contains spectral-normalization parameters such as original weights and power-iteration vectors while the destination model exposes ordinary weight keys.
failure_signature.root_cause: Spectral normalization changes the module parameterization and state-dictionary schema, but the destination model was constructed without applying the same parameterizations before loading.

steps: Create validation and full-data model instances through the same model factory.
Apply spectral normalization to the same modules in both instances before saving or loading state.
Verify that source and destination state-dictionary key sets match before calling load_state_dict.
Load strictly after the schemas match, then proceed with full-data retraining or inference.
repair_action.summary: Create validation and full-data model instances through the same model factory.

nodes.title: recreate spectral-normalization parametrizations before checkpoint loading
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a spectrally normalized transformer or classifier checkpoint has normalization-specific keys that are missing from a newly constructed destination model.

failure_signature.pattern: Multi-scale image feature extraction indexes an intermediate activation as batch-by-token-by-channel, but a forward hook captured a two-dimensional pooled tensor or an incompatible tuple element.
failure_signature.root_cause: The hook assumes every selected vision-transformer layer returns token-level hidden states in the same structure, without normalizing tuple outputs or checking tensor rank.

steps: Inspect the documented output contract of each selected SigLIP2 transformer layer.
In the hook, unwrap tuple or structured outputs to the actual hidden-state tensor.
Check the captured tensor rank before removing a class token or pooling across tokens.
Pool only three-dimensional token tensors; handle already pooled two-dimensional embeddings directly or select a layer that exposes token states.
Run one image batch through every selected hook and verify the resulting feature widths before extracting the complete dataset.
repair_action.summary: Inspect the documented output contract of each selected SigLIP2 transformer layer.

nodes.title: validate transformer-hook output rank before token pooling
nodes.when_to_use: Use when SigLIP2 multi-layer feature extraction raises an indexing error at token slicing because a captured activation has only two dimensions.

failure_signature.pattern: Mixed-precision training crashes at scaler.scale(loss).backward after constructing a CUDA GradScaler through a deprecated namespace with an argument interpreted under the legacy constructor contract.
failure_signature.root_cause: The training loop mixes the modern device-aware AMP calling convention with the deprecated CUDA-specific GradScaler API.

steps: Use the device-aware torch.amp GradScaler API consistently with the CUDA device type.
Use the matching torch.amp autocast context in the same training loop.
Enable scaling only when the active device is CUDA, and use ordinary precision behavior otherwise.
Execute one complete optimizer step, including scale, backward, step, and update, before starting the full training schedule.
repair_action.summary: Use the device-aware torch.amp GradScaler API consistently with the CUDA device type.

nodes.title: keep mixed-precision scaler and autocast APIs internally consistent
nodes.when_to_use: Use when Phase 1 CUDA training emits an AMP deprecation warning and then fails because the GradScaler constructor received a device string through the legacy API.

failure_signature.pattern: XGBClassifier training aborts because fit receives early_stopping_rounds as an unsupported keyword before any validation metric is produced.
failure_signature.root_cause: The pipeline uses an early-stopping calling convention from a different XGBoost estimator version than the installed runtime.

steps: Inspect the installed XGBClassifier interface before constructing the cross-validation training call.
Move early-stopping configuration to the estimator constructor or supported callback mechanism for that interface, while retaining a validation eval_set.
If early stopping is unnecessary for the final full-data fit, omit it there because no independent validation set is available.
Run one fold and verify that evaluation metrics are recorded and fit completes before launching all folds.
repair_action.summary: Inspect the installed XGBClassifier interface before constructing the cross-validation training call.

nodes.title: configure XGBoost early stopping through the installed estimator interface
nodes.when_to_use: Use when multimodal features have been extracted successfully but XGBClassifier.fit rejects early_stopping_rounds as an unexpected keyword.

failure_signature.pattern: One mutable imputer is repeatedly fitted on margin, shape, and texture training groups, after which validation or test groups are transformed using only the state from the last fitted group.
failure_signature.root_cause: Reusing a single fitted transformer across semantically distinct feature groups overwrites its learned statistics and applies texture-derived preprocessing state to margin and shape inputs.

steps: Create a separate imputer for each of the margin, shape, and texture feature groups.
Fit each imputer only on its corresponding training split or training fold.
Transform the corresponding validation and test group with that same group's fitted imputer.
Apply the same per-group ownership rule to scalers, PCA models, and other stateful transformations.
Assert that every transformed group preserves its expected column count and is produced by the transformer fitted for that group.
repair_action.summary: Create a separate imputer for each of the margin, shape, and texture feature groups.

nodes.title: isolate fitted preprocessing state by feature group and split
nodes.when_to_use: Use when grouped leaf features are preprocessed separately but one transformer instance is refitted across groups before validation or test transformation.

failure_signature.pattern: Full-image validation or inference fails because a reconstructed image has dimensions derived from another sample and cannot be compared with or cropped to the current document.
failure_signature.root_cause: The patch pipeline assumes every document shares a single global height and width, although document images in this task can have different native dimensions.

steps: Record the native height and width of every image when loading it.
Create reconstruction and overlap-weight accumulators separately for each image using that image's dimensions.
Place or blend patches only within the current image's coordinate bounds.
Crop any padded reconstruction back to the recorded native dimensions before computing RMSE or generating predictions.
Assert that each reconstructed prediction and its clean target have identical shapes before metric computation.
repair_action.summary: Record the native height and width of every image when loading it.

nodes.title: reconstruct each document at its native dimensions
nodes.when_to_use: Use when dataset inspection finds multiple image dimensions or when full-image reconstruction produces prediction-target shape mismatches.

failure_signature.pattern: A U-Net forward pass fails at a decoder skip concatenation because the upsampled decoder feature and encoder feature have different spatial heights or widths.
failure_signature.root_cause: Input padding and decoder upsampling do not preserve the same spatial lattice through all encoder and decoder levels, so corresponding skip tensors are not spatially aligned.

steps: Determine the network's total downsampling factor from the number and stride of encoder stages.
Pad input images or patches so both spatial dimensions are divisible by that factor.
At every decoder stage, resize or symmetrically pad or crop the decoder feature to the exact spatial shape of the corresponding encoder feature before concatenation.
After the output layer, crop the prediction back to the original unpadded dimensions.
Run a forward-shape test on representative odd-sized and task-sized inputs before training.
repair_action.summary: Determine the network's total downsampling factor from the number and stride of encoder stages.

nodes.title: align U-Net decoder features with skip tensors before concatenation
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a U-Net or similar encoder-decoder reports unequal spatial sizes at torch.cat or when document dimensions are not naturally divisible by the complete downsampling factor.

failure_signature.pattern: A decoder or output convolution receives a tensor whose channel count differs from the layer's declared in_channels after upsampling and skip fusion.
failure_signature.root_cause: The architecture's channel bookkeeping does not match the forward path; a block is configured for a pre-concatenation or earlier-stage width even though the preceding decoder block emits a different number of channels.

steps: Write down the channel width emitted by every encoder, upsampling, concatenation, and decoder block.
For each concatenation, configure the following convolution for the sum of the participating channel widths.
Configure the output head from the actual width emitted by the final decoder block rather than from an earlier concatenated width.
Add assertions for expected channels at skip-fusion boundaries.
Execute a representative dummy forward pass before starting the training loop.
repair_action.summary: Write down the channel width emitted by every encoder, upsampling, concatenation, and decoder block.

nodes.title: derive U-Net convolution inputs from actual concatenated channel counts
nodes.when_to_use: Use when Conv2d reports an expected-versus-actual channel mismatch in a U-Net decoder or output head.

failure_signature.pattern: NAFNet construction fails before training because the runtime does not provide the requested two-dimensional LayerNorm module.
failure_signature.root_cause: The model depends on a normalization class that is unavailable in the installed PyTorch API, so encoder blocks cannot be instantiated.

steps: Check normalization-layer availability in the target runtime before constructing the model.

Replace the unavailable two-dimensional LayerNorm with an available channel-wise normalization implementation compatible with NCHW tensors, such as InstanceNorm2d or an explicit permutation-based LayerNorm wrapper.
Preserve the block's input and output channel count when substituting normalization.
Instantiate the complete NAFNet and run a dummy forward pass before patch training begins.
repair_action.summary: Check normalization-layer availability in the target runtime before constructing the model.

nodes.title: use an available channel-wise normalization implementation in NAFNet blocks
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a NAFNet-style denoiser fails during model construction because LayerNorm2d or an equivalent NCHW normalization class is unavailable.

failure_signature.pattern: Overlapping-patch inference fails while adding a predicted patch into a full-image accumulator because one tensor is on CUDA and the other is on CPU.
failure_signature.root_cause: Predicted patches are transferred between devices independently of the reconstruction and overlap-count tensors, violating the single-device requirement for tensor arithmetic.

steps: Choose one device for reconstruction accumulation before entering the inference loop.
If accumulating on CPU, detach and transfer each predicted patch to CPU before blending it into CPU prediction and weight accumulators.
If accumulating on GPU, allocate both prediction and weight accumulators on the model's device and transfer the completed reconstruction to CPU only after blending.
Ensure coordinate masks, blending weights, and count tensors use the same device as the accumulator.
Assert device equality immediately before each patch accumulation operation.
repair_action.summary: Choose one device for reconstruction accumulation before entering the inference loop.

nodes.title: keep patch predictions and reconstruction accumulators on one device
nodes.when_to_use: Use when test or validation reconstruction blends model outputs into full-image tensors and runtime errors report tensors on different devices.

failure_signature.pattern: Training initialization fails when constructing a linear warmup scheduler because its multiplicative start factor is zero or outside the scheduler's accepted interval.
failure_signature.root_cause: LinearLR represents learning rates as positive factors of the optimizer's base rate and requires the starting factor to be greater than zero and no greater than one.

steps: Set the warmup start factor to a small positive value within the scheduler's valid interval, such as 0.001 or 0.01.
Set the end factor to a valid value, normally 1.0, and use a positive warmup iteration count.
Construct the warmup scheduler before training and inspect its first and final warmup learning rates.
When chaining warmup with cosine decay, align scheduler milestones with the intended number of warmup epochs.
repair_action.summary: Set the warmup start factor to a small positive value within the scheduler's valid interval, such as 0.001 or 0.01.

nodes.title: configure linear learning-rate warmup with a valid positive start factor
nodes.when_to_use: Use when an image-denoising training pipeline uses LinearLR warmup and scheduler construction rejects start_factor=0 or another out-of-range factor.

failure_signature.pattern: LightGBM training fails because categorical features are identified by column names while the supplied training matrix is a NumPy array without column metadata.
failure_signature.root_cause: Converting a pandas feature frame to a NumPy array removes column names, so LightGBM cannot resolve name-based categorical_feature entries against the training matrix.

steps: Determine whether the matrix passed to LightGBM preserves pandas column names.
If training from a NumPy array, map each categorical feature to its stable integer column index.
Pass those indices through the categorical_feature argument of lgb.Dataset instead of placing feature names in model parameters.
Alternatively, preserve the pandas DataFrame and use the LightGBM-supported name-based categorical feature syntax consistently.
Verify that categorical references resolve against the final post-transformation feature order before training.
repair_action.summary: Determine whether the matrix passed to LightGBM preserves pandas column names.

nodes.title: Align LightGBM categorical references with the training matrix representation
nodes.when_to_use: Use when LightGBM reports that categorical_feature is not a number or cannot resolve categorical feature names, and the model input was converted to a NumPy array.

failure_signature.pattern: Validation features contain fare aggregates computed from the full labeled dataset before the train-validation split.
failure_signature.root_cause: Location-level mean, standard deviation, or count features derived from fare_amount include validation targets, allowing validation observations to influence their own predictors and producing an optimistically biased score.

steps: Create the train-validation split before computing any fare-derived location statistics.
Fit the location aggregation table using only the training partition.
Join the frozen training-derived aggregates onto validation and test rows without recomputing them.
For training rows, use out-of-fold aggregates or leave-one-out logic when self-inclusion would materially leak the row target.
Define fallback values from training-partition statistics for unseen or sparse locations.
repair_action.summary: Create the train-validation split before computing any fare-derived location statistics.

nodes.title: Fit target-derived location aggregates only from the training partition
nodes.when_to_use: Use when features aggregate fare_amount or another target by rounded coordinates, geographic cells, routes, or location clusters and validation is performed on a held-out partition.

failure_signature.pattern: A numeric scaler is fitted on validation observations, either by concatenating train and validation data or by scaling the complete dataset before fold selection.
failure_signature.root_cause: The fitted means and variances incorporate the held-out distribution, violating validation isolation and biasing preprocessing toward data that should remain unseen.

steps: Create the temporal holdout or cross-validation fold indices before fitting the scaler.
Fit StandardScaler or the selected transformer only on numeric columns from the active training partition.
Use the fitted transformer without refitting to transform validation and test numeric columns.
Repeat scaler fitting independently for every cross-validation fold.
Keep categorical identifiers unscaled when the downstream model treats them as categorical features.
repair_action.summary: Create the temporal holdout or cross-validation fold indices before fitting the scaler.

nodes.title: Fit numeric scaling independently within each training partition
nodes.when_to_use: Use when validation or fold rows contribute to fit, fit_transform, or preprocessing statistics used by the corresponding training partition.

failure_signature.pattern: Validation error grows rapidly during XGBoost training on log-transformed fares, and inverse transformation with expm1 produces infinity values that break metric computation.
failure_signature.root_cause: An unstable regression objective and unconstrained boosting produce extreme log-scale predictions; exponentiating those predictions overflows floating-point range.

steps: Replace the unstable objective with reg:squarederror for log-fare regression.
Monitor validation RMSE and enable early stopping so training terminates when held-out performance stops improving.
Use the best validated boosting iteration for validation and test inference.
Check predictions for finiteness and clip log-scale outputs to a fare-appropriate finite range before applying expm1.
After inverse transformation, verify that all predictions are finite before calculating RMSE or passing predictions to a residual model.
repair_action.summary: Replace the unstable objective with reg:squarederror for log-fare regression.

nodes.title: Stabilize log-fare boosting before inverse transformation
nodes.when_to_use: Use when XGBoost log-target training shows rapidly increasing validation RMSE or when expm1 of model outputs yields infinity or non-finite fare predictions.

failure_signature.pattern: Training succeeds, but validation crashes with CUDA out-of-memory when the complete multi-million-row validation matrix is passed through the neural network in one forward call.
failure_signature.root_cause: A full-partition validation forward pass materializes activations and outputs for millions of taxi rows simultaneously, exceeding GPU memory even though training itself uses manageable mini-batches.

steps: Wrap validation features in a DataLoader or equivalent bounded batch iterator.
Run validation under evaluation mode and a no-gradient or inference context.
Move one validation batch at a time to the GPU and release batch-local tensors after accumulating metric statistics.
Accumulate squared-error sums and observation counts incrementally instead of retaining all validation outputs on the GPU.
Reduce the validation batch size if peak memory remains above the device limit.
repair_action.summary: Wrap validation features in a DataLoader or equivalent bounded batch iterator.

nodes.title: Stream neural-network validation through bounded batches
nodes.when_to_use: Use when a neural model trains in mini-batches but evaluates the entire large validation partition in one GPU forward pass and fails during validation with CUDA memory exhaustion.

failure_signature.pattern: Submission validation reports fewer predictions than test rows because coordinate, passenger-count, or other plausibility filters were applied to the test set.
failure_signature.root_cause: Training-oriented outlier removal was reused for test preprocessing, deleting required test observations and breaking the one-prediction-per-input-row submission contract.

steps: Apply target and outlier row filtering only to labeled training data.
Retain the original test row count and row order throughout feature engineering and inference.
Convert invalid test inputs into missing or bounded feature values instead of dropping their rows.
Impute non-finite engineered test features using values learned from training data or stable feature-specific defaults.
Build the submission against the original test index or key and assert that its row count and ordering exactly match the original test file.
repair_action.summary: Apply target and outlier row filtering only to labeled training data.

nodes.title: Preserve every test row while handling invalid feature values
nodes.when_to_use: Use when cleaned test data has fewer rows than the original 9,914-row NYC taxi test set or submission validation reports inconsistent sample counts.

failure_signature.pattern: A pretrained transformer sequence-classification model raises TypeError during initialization because dropout-related settings are passed directly to from_pretrained even though the selected architecture accepts them only through its configuration.
failure_signature.root_cause: Dropout parameter names and constructor signatures vary across ModernBERT, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa implementations; configuration fields were incorrectly treated as universal model constructor arguments.

steps: Load the checkpoint configuration with AutoConfig.from_pretrained or the architecture-specific config class.
Set the dropout fields actually exposed by that configuration, such as classifier_dropout, hidden_dropout_prob, attention_probs_dropout_prob, dropout, or attention_dropout.
Instantiate the sequence-classification model with from_pretrained using the modified config and num_labels, without forwarding dropout fields as standalone constructor keywords.
Inspect or validate the selected configuration fields before starting cross-validation or full training.
repair_action.summary: Load the checkpoint configuration with AutoConfig.from_pretrained or the architecture-specific config class.

nodes.title: configure transformer dropout through the checkpoint configuration
nodes.when_to_use: Use when ModernBERT, DistilBERT, RoBERTa, or another Hugging Face sequence classifier fails before training with an unexpected dropout-related keyword argument.

failure_signature.pattern: A text classifier combining SBERT, TF-IDF, pooled transformer, or projected representations fails on its first forward pass because a linear, branch, or recurrent layer expects a hardcoded width different from the actual feature width.
failure_signature.root_cause: Feature dimensions were duplicated as constants in the model definition instead of being propagated from fitted vectorizers and encoder outputs; projection or concatenation changed the representation width without updating downstream layers.

steps: After fitting each feature extractor, read its actual output width from the resulting matrix or vectorizer vocabulary.
Pass semantic_dim, tfidf_dim, projection_dim, and other source dimensions explicitly into the model constructor.
Define each source projection with its source width, for example Linear(tfidf_dim, projection_dim), rather than deriving it from an unrelated hidden size.
Set downstream branch or recurrent input widths to the exact post-operation width: sum widths after concatenation and use the projected width after projection.
Add assertions before training that batch feature widths match their projection layers and that the fused tensor width matches every downstream branch.
repair_action.summary: After fitting each feature extractor, read its actual output width from the resulting matrix or vectorizer vocabulary.

nodes.title: derive every fusion-layer dimension from extracted feature tensors
nodes.when_to_use: Use when this author-classification pipeline combines variable-width TF-IDF or stylometric features with fixed-width sentence or transformer embeddings and reports a matrix-multiplication or recurrent input_size mismatch.

failure_signature.pattern: Validation cross-entropy remains finite, but manually computed multiclass log loss becomes NaN after the classifier emits probabilities equal to zero or one.
failure_signature.root_cause: The metric takes logarithms before enforcing a finite probability range, so exact zero probabilities produce negative infinity and subsequent aggregation produces NaN.

steps: Collect validation logits in evaluation mode and convert them to probabilities with a numerically stable softmax.
Clip probabilities to a fixed epsilon interval before any logarithm, for example [1e-15, 1 - 1e-15].
Renormalize every probability row after clipping so each row sums to one.
Compute multiclass log loss with a standard metric implementation and an explicit complete class-label ordering.
Reject non-finite metric values before checkpoint selection so NaN cannot be treated as an improvement.
repair_action.summary: Collect validation logits in evaluation mode and convert them to probabilities with a numerically stable softmax.

nodes.title: clip and renormalize class probabilities before multiclass log loss
nodes.when_to_use: Use when validation predictions for EAP, HPL, and MWS are finite but manual log-loss evaluation becomes NaN as transformer training grows highly confident.

failure_signature.pattern: Validation fails when a one-dimensional vector of integer class IDs is multiplied directly by the logarithm of an N-by-C probability matrix.
failure_signature.root_cause: The manual metric formula assumes one-hot targets, but the validation loader supplies class indices, producing incompatible target and probability shapes.

steps: Keep validation targets as integer class indices and pass them with the N-by-C probability matrix to a multiclass log-loss implementation with explicit labels.
If a manual formula is required, convert class indices to an N-by-C one-hot matrix using the same class ordering as the model outputs.
Assert that the probability matrix has one column for each of EAP, HPL, and MWS and that target IDs are within that ordering.
Perform validation metric computation once per epoch from the complete accumulated targets and predictions.
repair_action.summary: Keep validation targets as integer class indices and pass them with the N-by-C probability matrix to a multiclass log-loss implementation with explicit labels.

nodes.title: compute multiclass log loss from class indices with a compatible metric
nodes.when_to_use: Use when author labels have shape N, predicted probabilities have shape N-by-3, and validation crashes with a broadcasting error during log-loss calculation.

failure_signature.pattern: Training reports a strong best validation log loss, but evaluation after reloading the supposed best model is substantially worse on the same validation split.
failure_signature.root_cause: The retained best state or final evaluation path is not guaranteed to be an immutable, exact reproduction of the state and inference procedure used when the best score was recorded.

steps: Capture the best checkpoint as a deep CPU clone of every state_dict tensor or save it immediately to a checkpoint file.
Store the associated epoch, validation indices, label ordering, tokenizer settings, and best metric alongside the weights.
Reload the saved state with strict key checking into the same model configuration.
Call model.eval and run the identical validation inference function used during epoch scoring, including the same softmax, clipping, and class ordering.
Verify immediately after reload that the recomputed score matches the recorded best score within numerical tolerance before generating test predictions.
repair_action.summary: Capture the best checkpoint as a deep CPU clone of every state_dict tensor or save it immediately to a checkpoint file.

nodes.title: preserve and reload an immutable best-checkpoint state
nodes.when_to_use: Use when early stopping identifies a best author-classification epoch but the final score on the unchanged validation split degrades sharply after checkpoint restoration.

failure_signature.pattern: Loading a DeBERTa-v3 checkpoint through a DeBERTa-v1 model class produces an architecture warning followed by embedding or parameter size mismatches.
failure_signature.root_cause: The checkpoint declares a DeBERTa-v2/v3-compatible architecture, but the code forces construction through the incompatible DebertaModel class.

steps: Load the checkpoint with AutoConfig and inspect its declared model_type.
Use AutoModel or AutoModelForSequenceClassification so the library selects the checkpoint-compatible DeBERTa implementation.
Build any custom classification head from the hidden size reported by the loaded configuration.
Perform a small tokenized forward-pass smoke test before beginning stratified cross-validation.
repair_action.summary: Load the checkpoint with AutoConfig and inspect its declared model_type.

nodes.title: match the model loader class to the checkpoint architecture
nodes.when_to_use: Use when microsoft/deberta-v3-base or another DeBERTa-v3 checkpoint warns that a deberta-v2 model is being instantiated as deberta and then reports parameter-size mismatches.

failure_signature.pattern: The first mixed-precision forward pass fails because attention scores in float16 are masked with a large negative constant such as -1e9 that cannot be represented by the tensor dtype.
failure_signature.root_cause: A mask sentinel chosen for float32 was applied directly to half-precision attention scores, exceeding float16's finite range.

steps: Determine the attention score tensor dtype inside the pooling forward pass.
Replace the fixed -1e9 sentinel with a representable dtype-aware value such as torch.finfo(scores.dtype).min, or compute masking and softmax in float32.
Apply the padding mask before softmax and ensure each sample retains at least one unmasked token.
Run a mixed-precision forward and backward smoke test containing padded sequences before full training.
repair_action.summary: Determine the attention score tensor dtype inside the pooling forward pass.

nodes.title: use dtype-safe attention mask sentinels under mixed precision
nodes.when_to_use: Use when custom attention pooling for the author classifier runs under AMP and masked_fill raises an at::Half overflow error.

failure_signature.pattern: Transformer fine-tuning fails during the first epoch with an attempt to backward through a graph a second time while gradient checkpointing and mixed-precision scaling are enabled.
failure_signature.root_cause: The selected gradient-checkpointing path is incompatible with the loss and AMP backward behavior in this training implementation, causing checkpointed intermediates to be reused after release.

steps: Disable model gradient checkpointing for this training pipeline.
Use a smaller per-device microbatch and gradient accumulation to retain the desired effective batch size.
Ensure each optimizer update is driven by one scaled backward call per microbatch and that no loss tensor from a prior step is retained.
Run a short forward-backward optimizer-step test before starting the full training schedule.
repair_action.summary: Disable model gradient checkpointing for this training pipeline.

nodes.title: disable incompatible gradient checkpointing and reduce microbatch size
nodes.when_to_use: Use when DeBERTa fine-tuning for this task raises a repeated-backward or freed-tensor error only after gradient checkpointing is enabled with AMP.

failure_signature.pattern: Cross-validation fails on the first fold because XGBoost rejects gpu_hist and reports that only approx, auto, exact, and hist are valid tree methods.
failure_signature.root_cause: The training configuration assumes the legacy gpu_hist method is available, but the installed XGBoost build exposes a different set of tree methods.

steps: Inspect the installed XGBoost version and its supported tree-method and device parameters before cross-validation.
Use tree_method='hist' for the supported CPU path in this embedding classifier.
Remove incompatible GPU-specific tree-method parameters rather than mixing them with the CPU configuration.
Run a small first-fold training smoke test and confirm early-stopping metadata is available before launching all folds.
Use the resulting best boosting-round count consistently when retraining on the full author-classification data.
repair_action.summary: Inspect the installed XGBoost version and its supported tree-method and device parameters before cross-validation.

nodes.title: select an XGBoost tree method supported by the installed build
nodes.when_to_use: Use when XGBoost training over frozen transformer embeddings rejects gpu_hist before producing a fold metric.
